newsitem.title: PERU: Peru seeks to halve extreme poverty level by 2000.
newsitem.headline: Peru seeks to halve extreme poverty level by 2000.

text.p: The government said Thursday it hopes to halve by the year 2000 the estimated number of 4.4 million Peruvians living in extreme poverty.
"This means that by the year 2000 around 2.2 million poor people will have left that state," said a statement from Government Palace.
Peru's total population is just under 24 million.

"Since 1990, the government of President (Alberto) Fujimori has concentrated its efforts on economic development, trying to make this the real motor to promote social development, so we can help people in extreme poverty escape their situation," said Presidency Minister Daniel Hokama, whose post controls the state's social programs.
The government has said that 44 percent of its proposed 1997 budget, or 10.9 billion soles, will be used for social spending.
Opposition figures, however, say this figure disguises large bureaucratic costs, and accuse Fujimori's administration of neglecting the poor in favor of foreign debt payments.
